1. Roll Call
A. A meeting was held on the 1st floor in Conference Room A at 7:00 pm in City Hall. Commissioner Charles
  Braggs, District 1, serves as interim chairperson until further notice.
B. Attendees included:
 Charles Braggs, Commissioner District 1 & Acting as Chairperson
 Kip Rudd, Commissioner District 2
 Brett C.S. Roberts, Commissioner District 3
 Lois Hale, Commissioner District 4

 Lieutenant David Salcedo, City of Inglewood Police Department
 Louis Atwell, City of Inglewood Public Works Director/Assistant City Manager

2. Approval of Minutes
A. January 2023 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Roberts made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by Commissioner Rudd.
  All Commissioners approved the meeting minutes.

3. Unfinished Business
A. To amend the Residential Permit Parking Program on 95th Street between 8th Ave and 6th Ave: Ballots
  were mailed on February 7, 2023. The deadline to receive ballots is March 9, 2023. The City will provide
  updates on the results.

4. New Business: NONE

5. Resolution: NONE

6. Public Comments
A. A Crenshaw Boulevard resident mentioned that an increase in speeding has been observed. The concern
  is that this occurred near a school located at 8420 Crenshaw Boulevard. Changing driver behavior is
  having more cops to ticket. Lieutenant David Salcedo took information from the resident to see if more
  patrols can be implemented to monitor.
B. An Oak Street resident expressed concern about the City's parking permit program. His concerns are the
  added costs and added stress to the community from the parking situation. Finally, the resident informed
  the Parking and Traffic Commission that Eloy Morales, Councilor for District 3, has not communicated with
  the community after constant calls to withdraw the parking permit throughout the District.
C. A 98th Street resident informed the commission that the green signal light at Century Boulevard does not
  give drivers enough time to make a left turn at the intersection of Century Blvd and Hawthorne Boulevard.
  The resident added that same effect is observed at Century Blvd and Fir Avenue and Century Blvd and
  Grevillea Avenue. The resident shared that drivers are illegally making U-turns at the intersection of
  Century Blvd and Hawthorne Boulevard.

E. The Inglewood Avenue and 96th Street resident mentioned that an increase in speeding has been

7. Public Hearing
A. To amend the Residential Permit Parking District for all of District 5D

 The public notice was mailed on February 6, 2023 prior to the February PTC meeting. The Public Works
  Department received a few calls regarding the Public Hearing at the Parking and Traffic Commission
  Meeting for the Residential Permit Parking Program for District 5D. The following are comments from
  residents who are unable to attend. Each comment explains why the resident is or is not in favor of the
  Residential Parking Permit Program for District 5D.
  1. Resident No. 1 is in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   Without the program, it is difficult for residents to park. Multiple vehicles are using the right-of-way
  for sales or commercial purposes.
  2. Resident No. 2 (Arbor Vitae/Truro Ave) is not in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   Anyone should be able to park and welcome family members to their home without parking
  restrictions. There should be no reason to pay to park on the street.
  3. Resident No. 3 is in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   It is a relief for residents to avoid seeing non-residents occupying parking spaces. The residents
  do not want businesses to abuse resident parking spaces.
   If the program is removed, it will be inconvenient for residents to park.
  4. Resident No. 4 (Eucalyptus Avenue) is in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   Parking is a nightmare. The street is sometimes occupied by 16 vehicles parked for commercial
  purposes while residents cannot find a parking space.
   Vehicles block residents' driveways, making it impossible for residents to leave their homes.
   It is difficult to contact parking enforcement; it takes more than four hours for them to respond.
   The cost of an additional parking permit is not as expensive as in other cities.
  5. Resident No. 5 (Hardy & Eucalyptus Avenue) is in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   The program provides parking for residents’ families while they visit and businesses providing
  services to residents, such as gardening or construction. In addition, the program monitors non-
  resident vehicles that can be towed or ticketed. Parking Enforcement is helpful during sweeping
  days or when residents double park on the street.
   This program provides more parking opportunities.

  was implemented and that it does not want to experience again.
   The residents parked on the street instead of in their driveways. This caused residents to fight
  over parking spaces.
   Residents with rental units on their property added to the street parking issues.

   Car accidents took place on the street due to congestion.
   Non-residents park on the neighborhood streets and walk to the Stadium for events.

  7. Resident No. 7 (98th Street) is in favor of having Residential Permit Parking:
   The two hours allotted for parking in these residential areas for non-residents, which is ample time
  for visitors and guests, prevents unwanted strangers and non-residents from parking overnight.
   Parking permit prevents loitering and overnight parking of strangers. Residents want to be able to
  park in their own neighborhood with streets that are safe, clean, and uncluttered with unfamiliar
  cars.

 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given as to why the resident does or does not
  support the parking program:
  1. Residents rely heavily on street parking. The program is inconvenient and unreasonable.
  2. The family owned more than two vehicles and disagrees with the decision to pay additional permits just
  for street parking.
  3. Resident does not want to purchase for visitor parking.
  4. The Residential Permit Parking District Program does not allow residents to use their own permit to
  park in another area within the City of Inglewood. This gives an inconvenience when visiting friends,
  relatives and for business purposes.
  5. Rosewood Avenue resident does not want to eliminate District Residential Permit Parking Program in
  the neighborhood. The program had helped the community get cleaner and remove excess vehicles.
  The resident can find to park in the vicinity.
  6. Rosewood Avenue resident does not want to eliminate District Residential Permit Parking Program in
  the neighborhood. Residents from Century Boulevard to Hardy Street in Rosewood Avenue filed a
  petition to maintain the program. The document can be found as an attachment to these meeting
  minutes for reference.
  7. Maple Street resident does not want to eliminate District Residential Permit Parking Program in the
  neighborhood. Streets feel safer and cleaner. Business visitors park less, but call for increased parking
  enforcement to ensure resident parking. Residents from Century Boulevard to Hardy Street in Maple
  Street filed a petition to maintain the program. The document can be found as an attachment to these
  meeting minutes for reference.

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Terminate Residential Permit Parking Program for 95th Street
  between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue

RECOMMENDATION:
It is requested that the Parking and Traffic Commission review the information included in this
report and approve the resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program within
District 7C at 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue.

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program that was in effect
24 hours a day, 7 days a week with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
(Ordinace No. 20-09). The program was adopted to more effectively and efficiently protect the
residential communities from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On February 14, 2022, Public Works Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking for 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue. The Public
Works Department staff received and reviewed the petition. Eighteen (18) valid signatures were
submitted on the petition, resulting in seventy-five percent (75%) of all households on the block
signing the petition in favor of removing permit parking restrictions.

DISCUSSION:
On January 26, 2023, the Parking and Traffic Commission held a public hearing on the issue of
terminating the Residential Permit Parking Program for District 7C for 95th Street between 8th
Avenue and 6th Avenue. The Public Works Department requested that the Parking and Traffic
Commission listen to public comments and provide direction on whether the petition should go
to a vote by the residents. As a result, all district commissioners voted to approve the request
to begin the voting process.

On February 7, 2023, the Public Works Department mailed questionaries to each resident
residing in the boundary area of the petition and were requested to return the questionnaires
within thirty (30) calendar days. March 9, 2023 was the deadline to take questionnaires. On
March 13, 2023, the questionnaires were counted. Eighteen (18) votes were cast to approve
the termination, while one (1) vote opposed the termination of the Residential Permit Parking
Program. Based on the number of votes received, ninety-five percent (95%) of households
supported the approval to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program for District 7C for
95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue.

For the parking restrictions to be removed, a minimum of seventy-five percent (75%) of the

residents, Public Works staff recommends that the Parking and Traffic Commission approve the
resolution to terminate the Residential Permit Parking Program for District 7C for 95th Street
between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue.

Subject:  Vote to Approve or Reject the termination of Residential Permit Parking for

The purpose of this letter is to allow residents the opportunity to vote on the removal of the
Residential Permit Parking for 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue within District
7C. By voting "approve", this street will not be subject to the rules of a Residential Permit
Parking District. By voting "reject", this street will continue to have permitted parking and follow
the rules associated with it. The complete rules and procedures can be found in the Inglewood
Municipal Code Section 3-76 (Establishment of a Permit Parking District) through Section 3-76.1
(Amending or Terminating a Permit Parking District).

Since the Parking and Traffic Commission has determined that permitted parking may not be
warranted in the area in question, ballots are mailed to all residences on the street described
above.

If seventy-five percent (75%) or more of respondents vote “approve” for the termination of
Residential Permit Parking, then an ordinance amending the Residential Permit Parking District
will be submitted to the City Council for consideration. If approved, 95th Street between 8th
Avenue and 6th Avenue within District 7C will not be subject to the Residential Permit Parking
District rules. Therefore, all vehicles can park on these streets without showing a parking permit
at all hours of the day, every day of the week. Additionally, the current parking prohibitions for
street sweeping will remain unchanged.

Using the enclosed ballot, please vote to approve or reject the termination of the Residential
Permit Parking District on 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue within District 7C.
Please return the ballot to the City of Inglewood Public Works Department within the next thirty
(30) days. Only one vote per household will be accepted. If you have any questions, please
don't hesitate to get in touch with the Public Works Department, at (310) 412-5333.

Tema:  Vote para Aprobar o Rechazar la terminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento Residencial para 95th Street entre 8th Avenue y 6th
  Avenue dentro del Distrito 7C

El propósito de esta carta es brindarles a los residentes la oportunidad de votar sobre la
eliminación del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial para 95th Street entre 8th Avenue y
6th Avenue dentro del Distrito 7C. Al votar "aprobar", esta calle no estará sujeta a las reglas de
un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial. Al votar "rechazar", esta calle seguirá
teniendo estacionamiento permitido y seguirá las reglas asociadas. Las reglas y procedimientos
completos se pueden encontrar en el Código Municipal de Inglewood, Sección 3-76
(Establecimiento de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso) hasta la Sección 3-76.1
(Modificación o Terminación de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso).

Dado que la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico ha determinado que es posible que no se
justifique el estacionamiento permitido en el área en cuestión, las boletas se envían por correo
a todas las residencias en la calle descrita anteriormente.

Si el setenta y cinco por ciento (75%) o más de los encuestados votan "aprueban" la
terminación del permiso de estacionamiento residencial, entonces se presentará una
ordenanza que modifica el Distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial al Concejo
Municipal para su consideración. Si se aprueba, 95th Street entre 8th Avenue y 6th Avenue
dentro del Distrito 7C no estará sujeta a las reglas del Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso
Residencial. Por lo tanto, todos los vehículos pueden estacionar en estas calles sin mostrar un

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
Residential Permit Parking within District 7C at 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday January 25th, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may
attend this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an
opportunity to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking on 95th Street between 8th Avenue and 6th Avenue is severely impacted in this manner
and if the elimination of a Residential Permit Parking District would be warranted. If it is determined to
be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the proposed parking district. A 75-
percent (75 %) approval is required to eliminate a Residential Permit Parking District.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de

Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la
cancelación del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7C en 95th Street entre
8th Avenue y 6th Avenue. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de
Inglewood, este asunto se presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la
hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 25 de Enero de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en
cuestión. Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del
Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los
residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios
de estacionamiento disponibles en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad
de estacionamiento en la calle en 95th Street entre 8th Avenue y 6th Avenue se ve gravemente
afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la eliminación de un Distrito de Estacionamiento con
Permiso Residencial. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada
hogar dentro del distrito de estacionamiento propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del 75 por ciento
(75 %) para eliminar un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial.

Si se elimina un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no se restringirá el
estacionamiento en las calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún
momento; incluso durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea
expresar una opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento
de Obras Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.

SUBJECT: Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 77th Street
  between 8th Avenue and 7th Avenue

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing
to do the following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of Residential Permit Parking
  Program for 77th Street between 8th Ave and 7th Ave within District 7B; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The
program is enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday
through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted
to protect residential communities more effectively and efficiently from non-resident
vehicle intrusion.

On April 26, 2022, Public Works Department received a petition requesting the
removal of Residential Permit Parking for 77th Street between 8th Avenue and 7th
Avenue. The Public Works Department staff received and reviewed the petition.
Seventeen (17) valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) were submitted
on the petition, resulting in seventy-one percent (71%) of all households on the block
signing the petition in favor of removing permit parking restrictions.

DISCUSSION:
Residential Permit Parking Districts encourage residents to use their driveways, when
available, to park their vehicles so that those without driveways can park on the street.
Since the District's creation, residents have had more parking opportunities in the
District. Public Works staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission provide
instructions to staff on how to proceed with the request by either:
1. Approve the request to start the voting process; or
2. Deny the request to end the processing of the petition.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
Residential Permit Parking within District 7B at 77th Street between 8th Avenue and 7th Avenue. Per
Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the Inglewood
Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday April 26, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some on-
street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a nearby
commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-street
parking is severely impacted in this manner and if the termination of a Residential Permit Parking within
District 7B at 77th Street between 8th Avenue and 7th Avenue would be warranted. If it is determined to
be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the proposed parking district. A 75-percent
(75 %) approval is required to eliminate a Residential Permit Parking District.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will not
be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you have any
questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the public hearing,
please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 77th Street entre la 8th Avenue y 7th
Avenue. De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se
presentará a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 26 de Abril de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en cuestión.
Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del Programa
de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los residentes de algunos
espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde los clientes y/o empleados
de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de estacionamiento disponibles
en la calle.

La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de
estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la terminación de
un Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 7B en 77th Street entre 8th Avenue y 7th
Avenue. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del
distrito de estacionamiento propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del 75 por ciento (75 %) para eliminar
un distrito de estacionamiento con permiso residencial.

Si se elimina un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no se restringirá el estacionamiento
en las calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún momento; incluso
durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una opinión
pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas de
